utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good afternoon ladies and gentlemen. As I indicated yesterday, the Trial Chamber shall read this short ruling. After I have just read the conclusion, the Registrar will try and get you the copies, because they are not quite ready. And this is a preliminary decision, we will have to write a full decision. Now, on the 24th July, '98 the Trial Chamber heard the Prosecution's application for a proposed rebuttal of the Defence case. The Trial Chamber, having listened to arguments, was of the opinion that only Dr. Landy Sparr, the expert witness on the medical evidence of Esad Landzo, could be called as a rebuttal witness. We held the view that the evidence of the remaining witnesses, namely Rajko Djordjic, Stephen Chambers and Professor Andreja Stegnar, did not constitute true rebuttal evidence but may only be regarded as fresh evidence. On the 28th of July, 1998 the Trial Chamber answered affirmatively to the inquiry of the Prosecution, whether it could file an application to reopen its case to enable it to call the three witnesses who the Trial Chamber held did not meet the parameters of rebuttal evidence. The Prosecution has now brought this application, filed on the 30th July, 1998 to reopen this case. It still maintains that all of the witnesses proposed and documents sought to be admitted are within the permissible ambit of rebuttal evidence. Now, I dealt extensively with the arguments of counsel. I don't think I have enough breath to read all these things now. However, I came to a conclusion which I thought was the only necessary thing for the purpose of this decision. The conclusion that the Trial Chamber came to is that the evidence suggested as rebuttal evidence do not come within the purview of such evidence as discussed in this decision. The new evidence put forward are evidence which existed ab initio and did not arise ex improviso. The failure to obtain them during the presentation of the case of the Prosecution has not been satisfactorily explained. On the representation of the Prosecution the Trial Chamber has no doubts the trial will be further protracted by the admission of the evidence. In any event, the evidence is founded on inference and cannot be said to point unequivocally at the establishing of the case of the Prosecution. In our view the justice of the case and the fair and expeditious trial of the proceedings enjoys a rejection of the application. This is the decision of the Trial Chamber. I think that's all we have for the proceedings of the day. So the Trial Chamber will now rise.
